lines.text: Which ball lands first? One thrown sideways, one just dropped.
lines.phonemes: wˌɪtʃ bˈɔːl lˈændz fˈɜːst? wˈʌn θɹˈoʊn sˈaɪdweɪz, wˈʌn dʒˈʌst dɹˈɑːpt.

lines.text: Here's a drop, slowed twenty times. Ghosts every twentieth of a second, and the gaps keep growing: a falling ball speeds up the whole way down.
lines.phonemes: hˈɪɹz ɐ dɹˈɑːp, slˈoʊd twˈɛnti tˈaɪmz. ɡˈoʊsts ˈɛvɹi twˈɛntiəθ əvə sˈɛkənd, ænd ðə ɡˈæps kˈiːp ɡɹˈoʊɪŋ: ɐ fˈɔːlɪŋ bˈɔːl spˈiːdz ˌʌp ðə hˈoʊl wˈeɪ dˈaʊn.

lines.text: Now throw one sideways from the same height, at the same instant. It sails twenty centimeters across… and lands on the same frame.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ θɹˈoʊ wˈʌn sˈaɪdweɪz fɹʌmðə sˈeɪm hˈaɪt, æt ðə sˈeɪm ˈɪnstənt. ɪt sˈeɪlz twˈɛnti sˈɛntɪmˌiːɾɚz əkɹˈɑːs… ænd lˈændz ɔnðə sˈeɪm fɹˈeɪm.

lines.text: Gravity pulls both balls down the same way. In sixteen thirty-eight, Galileo described a throw as two motions: a steady glide across, plus a fall. So at every tick, both sit at the same height.
lines.phonemes: ɡɹˈævᵻɾi pˈʊlz bˈoʊθ bˈɔːlz dˌaʊn ðə sˈeɪm wˈeɪ. ɪn sˈɪkstiːn θˈɜːɾiˈeɪt, ɡˌælɪlˈeɪoʊ dᵻskɹˈaɪbd ɐ θɹˈoʊ æz tˈuː mˈoʊʃənz: ɐ stˈɛdi ɡlˈaɪd əkɹˈɑːs, plˈʌs ɐ fˈɔːl. sˌoʊ æɾ ˈɛvɹi tˈɪk, bˈoʊθ sˈɪt æt ðə sˈeɪm hˈaɪt.

lines.text: Throw twice as hard, then three times: forty centimeters out, then sixty. Every row of ghosts stays level, and all four land on the same frame.
lines.phonemes: θɹˈoʊ twˈaɪs æz hˈɑːɹd, ðˈɛn θɹˈiː tˈaɪmz: fˈɔːɹɾi sˈɛntɪmˌiːɾɚz ˈaʊt, ðˈɛn sˈɪksti. ˈɛvɹi ɹˈoʊ ʌv ɡˈoʊsts stˈeɪz lˈɛvəl, ænd ˈɔːl fˈɔːɹ lˈænd ɔnðə sˈeɪm fɹˈeɪm.

lines.text: Measure it: nine gaps of a twentieth of a second. A one-meter fall takes about point four five seconds, thrown or dropped.
lines.phonemes: mˈɛʒɚɹ ɪt: nˈaɪn ɡˈæps əvə twˈɛntiəθ əvə sˈɛkənd. ɐ wˈʌnmˈiːɾɚ fˈɔːl tˈeɪks ɐbˌaʊt pˈɔɪnt fˈɔːɹ fˈaɪv sˈɛkəndz, θɹˈoʊn ɔːɹ dɹˈɑːpt.

lines.text: Sideways speed changes where a ball lands, not when. For a level throw, only the height sets the clock.
lines.phonemes: sˈaɪdweɪz spˈiːd tʃˈeɪndʒᵻz wˌɛɹ ɐ bˈɔːl lˈændz, nˌɑːt wˈɛn. fɚɹə lˈɛvəl θɹˈoʊ, ˈoʊnli ðə hˈaɪt sˈɛts ðə klˈɑːk.

lines.text: Next: why big swings and small swings take almost the same time.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: wˌaɪ bˈɪɡ swˈɪŋz ænd smˈɔːl swˈɪŋz tˈeɪk ˈɔːlmoʊst ðə sˈeɪm tˈaɪm.
